hero.title: Your F&B should work, regardless of who is in the kitchen.
hero.description: We make your hotel's F&B independent of individuals and profitable. Built as a system, led by a head chef, drawing on the experience of every property we work with.

dasProblem.title: As long as F&B depends on one person, it's your biggest risk.
dasProblem.description: In most properties, the kitchen stands or falls with the person at the stove. When they leave, quality suffers — and the search starts over. Good kitchen expertise is becoming increasingly rare and expensive. A single property can barely afford it on its own. This makes F&B the greatest lever for profitability — and at the same time the greatest source of uncertainty.

stufe1.title: Stage 1: The F&B System Check
stufe1.description: The starting point of every collaboration. We analyze location, numbers, and competition and show you which system works at your property. Clear recommendation, fixed price.

whatsDone.title: Before the Visit
whatsDone.text: We request a few key figures: P&L, food cost, labor costs, menus, and footfall data. The analysis starts before we arrive.

whatsDone.title: On-Site, One Day
whatsDone.text: We walk through the kitchen and outlets, look at the workflows, and speak with management. This gives us the picture that numbers alone cannot show.

whatsDone.title: Evaluation
whatsDone.text: We consolidate everything into a clear diagnosis — with benchmarking, location analysis, and risk check. From this comes the path recommendation and an initial profitability calculation.

stufe1.youGetIntro: A written results document and a meeting to go through it together. The document shows:
youGetItems: Where your F&B stands economically, based on the key ratios.

The recommended path — system kitchen, hybrid, or robotic — with reasoning.
An initial profitability calculation with achievable food cost ratio, staffing logic, and rough investment framework.
The next step, with a rough framework for the build phase.
stufe1.youGetFooter: You leave the check with a decision basis, not a gut feeling.
stufe1.notIncludedText: No finished concept, no recipes, no detailed costing, no supplier or technology selection, no implementation. That is Stage 2, the build. This clear boundary makes the build the logical next step.

modal.headline: Robotic Gastronomy – a new operating system for gastronomy.
modal.intro1: Gastronomy is facing a structural transformation. Over 60,000 open positions, rising labor costs, and growing margin pressure make it clear: the existing operating model is reaching its limits.
modal.intro2: Robotic Gastronomy is the answer. Not as a single technology, but as an integrated operating system built on four pillars:

pillars.title: Automation
pillars.text: Robotics takes over recurring processes in the kitchen, logistics, and service. The result: consistent quality, less dependency on staff, predictable workflows.

pillars.title: Digitalization
pillars.text: Fully networked systems connect ordering, production, and guest retention. Every process becomes measurable and controllable.

pillars.title: AI Integration
pillars.text: Artificial intelligence enables forecasts for revenue, cost of goods, and expenses. Planning replaces gut feeling.

pillars.title: Scalability
pillars.text: Together, these disciplines make gastronomy reproducible – across locations, without complexity and costs growing proportionally.

modal.outro1: Cooking robotics is already being used today by companies such as REWE, Mercedes-Benz, and the German armed forces. The market is growing at around 20% annually. The technology is available – what has been missing so far are business models that integrate it economically.
modal.outro2: This is exactly where Robotic Gastronomy comes in: technology not as an end in itself, but as the foundation for gastronomy that works economically – for operators, investors, and guests.

ways.title: Way 1: Hybrid Kitchen
ways.description: A hybrid kitchen connects the standardised workflows of a system kitchen with targeted à-la-carte elements. Recurring production steps run via technology and fixed standards, while the team focuses on individual components, quality, and the guest experience. This creates the bridge between classic à-la-carte and system kitchen.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: When staff is scarce but a full system kitchen is not yet economically or conceptually feasible.

whenNot.label: When it does not
whenNot.text: When the existing infrastructure does not allow for adaptation.

ways.title: Way 2: System Kitchen
ways.description: A system kitchen is fully standardised. All production runs via a few clearly defined kitchen appliances, and all workflows, recipes, and processes are documented in fixed standards (SOPs). The result: consistent quality, predictable costs, and low dependency on individuals — because knowledge lives in the system, not just in individual heads.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: For properties with fluctuating business that still want to bring quality and profitability to a reliable level.

whenNot.label: When it does not
whenNot.text: When you do not want to change your existing structures and workflows.

ways.title: Way 3: Robotic
ways.description: Robotic means consistent automation for round-the-clock operations. Robots handle food preparation fully automatically, embedded in a well-thought-out business model with clearly defined workflows. Important: robotics is not an end in itself or a gimmick, but a lever for productivity and growth.

whenUseful.label: When it makes sense
whenUseful.text: For locations with constant volume and round-the-clock demand, such as supplying employees and guests.

My name is Tim Plasse. My journey in gastronomy was not a straight line upward. It was shaped by glorious openings, but also by painful moments of failure.
